apt-controls: An APT 600 lane is the one we meet most often on a flat staff car park. The APT 950 is the wider APT Controls entrance, and the boom is longer, so the spring and the loop positions change. Tell us which badge is on the door.
APT Controls booms are ordered to the measured opening, not to a photograph taken at an angle. If the APT 600 arm has been cut down on site, we measure what is left before a replacement is cut.
Loop tails for an APT Controls cabinet are labelled before they are lifted. A loop that was paved over is a civils conversation, not a promise made from the car park office.
When an APT Controls barrier shares a post with a pedestrian gate, the quote says whether the gate closer is included. We do not take the gate off to make the boom look straight.

Staff who use an APT 600 every morning care more about a predictable raise than about a brochure. We time three APT 600 cycles with the lane empty and write the seconds down. If an APT 950 has a skirt fitted, the skirt stays in the measurement because it changes the inertia of that longer APT arm. Paving joints over an APT loop are photographed so a later cut knows where the wire runs. The APT cabinet key is returned to the person who met us, not left in the lock.
atg-access: ATG Access work is usually a blocker or a bollard, not a lightweight parking arm. The foundation, the hydraulic pack and the rising time are the survey. A cosmetic boom swap is the wrong description for an ATG Access product.

If an ATG blocker has been left down after a power cut, we ask when it last completed a raise. The oil level, the hose and the control key are checked before anyone talks about a new ATG Access cabinet.
Pedestrian routes beside an ATG Access blocker are drawn on the note. People step around a half-raised blade. That is written as a safety point, not as a styling comment.
Spare seals and hoses for ATG Access plant are confirmed against the unit on site. We do not bring a generic car-park spring and call it an ATG part.

An ATG blocker that serves a goods yard spends its life under lorries, so the pit collects mud. We measure the mud depth before quoting an ATG seal kit. Rising time is taken with a stopwatch from the ATG control point the driver actually uses, which is sometimes a button in a hut and not the cabinet. If pedestrians have worn a path across the ATG foundation, that path is in the note as a reason to pause the test while people pass. Hydraulic leaks are traced to the hose number, not described as the whole ATG machine failing.
avon-barrier: Avon Barrier arms and Avon bollards are identified separately. A site can have both. The quote names which Avon product is being serviced so a bollard invoice is not written up as an arm.
An Avon arm that stops at forty-five degrees is often a spring, a limit, or something blocking the arc. We watch the arc with the lane empty before the Avon cabinet is condemned.
Avon bollards need a clear sleeve. Grit, a bent lid or a flooded pit is recorded with a depth, because that decides whether the Avon unit can be lifted on the day.
The Avon handover lists the key numbers the site already uses. We do not re-pin an Avon lock and take the only key away.

Avon sites often mix an arm at the car entrance with bollards at the side gate. We label the Avon arm as lane A and each Avon bollard by its pit number so the invoice cannot swap them. A bent Avon bollard lid is a separate line from a dead Avon arm motor. Residents who walk dogs through the Avon line are asked which hour is quiet enough for a test. The Avon override key is tried by the building manager while we watch, and we only adjust a limit if they agree the parked position is wrong.
dea: DEA lanes are parking operators. The call is usually a DEA cabinet that has locked the car park at the end of the day. We ask which reader or ticket machine sits beside the DEA barrier before the visit.
A DEA boom lying on the ground is made safe first. The cause, a snapped bolt or a sprung gearbox, is photographed on the DEA chassis so the replacement matches the bolt pattern.
Season tickets and free-exit loops on a DEA lane are tested with the site's own card if they will lend it. We do not invent a pass to prove the DEA reader.
DEA manuals stay with the building. If the previous maintainer took them, the note says the DEA model was identified from the plate alone.

DEA car parks usually have a pay station within sight of the arm. We stand where the driver stands, not only at the DEA door. A DEA ticket jam and a DEA arm fault are written as two jobs even when they happened on the same evening. The free-exit loop, if the DEA lane has one, is tested with a car rolling at walking pace. Night-time DEA complaints about a dark boom are passed to the lighting circuit, and we say so rather than fitting a brighter DEA LED that was not asked for.

A DEA lane that fails at closing time is usually the reader, the ticket column or the arm, and those are written as three lines. The person who calls from the pay station often says the barrier is dead when the DEA column has rejected the ticket and the arm has not been asked to move. We stand at the DEA column with them and watch one ticket before the DEA housing is opened. If the DEA column accepts the ticket and the arm stays down, the input at the DEA controller is the next check, and the DEA spring is left alone.

Season tickets on a DEA lane are tested with a card the site lends us for one pass. We do not keep the card, and we do not invent a DEA pass to prove the reader. The result is the time, the card type they named, and whether the DEA arm completed the raise. A free-exit loop, where the DEA lane has one, is tested with a car rolling at walking pace, not by walking the loop. Walking a DEA loop can show a healthy detector that will still miss a low car, so the note says which vehicle was used.

Night complaints about a dark DEA boom are passed to the lighting circuit. We do not fit a brighter DEA lamp that was not asked for and then call the lane repaired. If the DEA arm itself is the dark object and the site wants a strip, that strip is a separate line on the quote. The DEA gearbox price is not used to hide a lighting request. The quote names the DEA lane, the column and whether the arm moved.

Bolt patterns on a DEA chassis are photographed before a boom is ordered. A DEA boom lying on the ground is made safe first, and the photograph shows the broken bolt or the sprung gearbox so the replacement matches that chassis rather than a boom from a different DEA generation. If the previous maintainer took the DEA manual, the model is taken from the plate and the note says so. We do not guess a DEA part number from the colour of the housing.

DEA equipment already on a car park is serviced or replaced on its own quote. That is not a DEA partnership. CAME is the barrier partner we specify when a lane is being built new. A DEA barrier that is already in the ground stays a DEA barrier until the operator asks for a different machine. Price is on application after the lane, the reader and the safety devices are known. You get that quote before the DEA lane is taken out of use. The office is 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport SK2 5DE. Call or WhatsApp 07517 806082 or email icomplypropertyservices@gmail.com.

The DEA handover is one exit watched by the operator. We do not leave a DEA arm parked upright to make the morning quieter unless they have asked for that. If two DEA lanes share a nest, they are surveyed as a pair, and a DEA arm that opens because the other lane's loop is occupied is a nesting fault. We do not price a new DEA boom for a nesting fault. The person who locks the car park is shown the DEA release, and they operate it once before we leave so the night close is not a mystery.

A DEA ticket jam and a DEA arm fault are written as two jobs even when they happened on the same evening. The free written quote names both or it names the one we found. Staff who use the DEA lane every morning care more about a predictable raise than about a brochure, so we time three cycles with the lane empty and leave the seconds with the building. Paving joints over a DEA loop are photographed so a later cut knows where the wire runs. The DEA cabinet key is returned to the person who met us, not left in the lock.
designa: Designa is a parking system as much as a barrier. The ticket, the barrier and the exit column have to agree. A Designa arm that moves while the column rejects every ticket is a logic fault, not a spring fault.
We ask for a Designa shift report or a photograph of the rejected ticket. The time on the ticket and the time on the Designa barrier log are compared before parts are blamed.
Nesting and tariff changes are the car park operator's settings. We do not rewrite a Designa tariff. We say when the barrier is healthy and the complaint is the tariff.
A Designa lane closed with a cone is reopened only when the safety loop sees a vehicle again. The operator watches one exit with us.

Designa offices judge a lane by the shift screen, so we ask them to open that screen before we touch the Designa arm. A rejected Designa ticket is bagged and the time is copied onto the note. If the Designa column accepts the ticket and the arm still waits, the input wire is the suspect, and the Designa spring is left alone. Tariff buttons are not our job. We will say the Designa barrier is healthy when the only change the office wants is a price on the ticket.

A Designa exit that works for staff fobs and refuses visitor tickets is written as a Designa validation rule, not as a failed Designa gearbox. We ask the operator to run one known-good ticket and one rejected ticket while we watch the Designa column, and both results go on the note with the time. The Designa barrier is left in the position the car park needs overnight. We do not park a Designa arm upright to make the morning quieter unless the manager has asked for that. Power to the Designa column is identified before any cover comes off, because a dark screen and a dead arm are different faults and the quote says which one we found.

Designa lanes that share a nest with a second barrier are surveyed as a pair. A Designa arm that opens because the other lane's loop is occupied is a nesting fault, and we do not price a new Designa boom for it. The manager stands at the Designa pay station for one full exit so they can see the same screen we see. If the Designa ticket printer is out of paper, that is written as a consumable, not as a barrier repair. The free written quote names the Designa lane, the column and whether the arm itself was the fault. CAME remains the barrier partner we specify for a new lane. Designa equipment already on site is serviced or replaced. That is not a Designa partnership.
eagle: Eagle barriers on older yards often have a boom that has been tied vertically for months. We ask why it was tied. An Eagle photocell wrapped in tape is unwrapped only after the reason is written down.
The Eagle spring is matched to the boom that is fitted now, including any sign or skirt someone has added. A heavier Eagle arm needs the spring the plate allows, not the spring that was in the van.
Manual release on an Eagle cabinet is demonstrated to the person who locks the yard. They turn it. We do not leave an Eagle release that only an engineer can find.
Painted-over Eagle rating plates are cleaned enough to read the model. If the plate is gone, the Eagle gearbox casting is photographed and the quote waits for that identification.

Eagle yards on industrial estates are often locked by the last person to leave, who is not a barrier engineer. We ask that person to show the Eagle release before we service anything, because they will be the one using it at 7pm. Tape on an Eagle photocell is removed only with their say-so and the reason they taped it is written first. An Eagle boom that has lived vertically for a season may have taken a set; we say if the Eagle arm needs replacing rather than pretending a new spring will straighten it.

An Eagle boom that has been tied vertically is a question before it is a repair. We ask who tied it and why, and that reason is written before any tape comes off an Eagle photocell. Sites tie an Eagle photocell because it was nuisance-tripping on weeds, on a trailer, or on a gate that swings through the beam. Removing the tape without writing the reason puts the same fault back the next windy day. The Eagle photocell is cleaned and aimed only when the person who locks the yard agrees.

The Eagle spring is matched to the boom that is fitted now. A sign, a skirt or a length of advertising banner changes the weight. We do not fit the Eagle spring that happened to be in the van and then adjust the limits until the arm just about rises. If the Eagle plate does not allow the spring the present boom needs, the quote says the boom or the spring has to change, and which one. An Eagle arm that has taken a set from living vertically for a season is described as a bent arm. A new spring will not straighten it.

Manual release on an Eagle cabinet is demonstrated to the person who actually locks the yard, who is often not a barrier engineer. They turn it. We do not leave an Eagle release that only the visiting engineer can find behind a cover. The position of that release is written in plain words, not as a diagram they will not keep. If the Eagle key is the only one and it lives on a bunch with the roller-shutter keys, we say so, and we do not take it away.

Painted-over Eagle rating plates are cleaned enough to read the model. If the plate is gone, the Eagle gearbox casting is photographed and the quote waits for that identification. Ordering an Eagle boom from a photograph taken across the yard is how the wrong length arrives. We measure the opening and the arm that is there, including any piece that has already been cut down. The Eagle note records both numbers.

Eagle barriers on older industrial yards are often the only control the last person trusts at the end of the shift. The quote says whether the Eagle lane can stay in manual use while a part is ordered. We do not lock an Eagle arm in a position the yard cannot live with overnight. Price is on application after the spring, the photocells and the release have been seen. CAME is the partner we specify when a lane is new. An Eagle barrier that is already installed is serviced or replaced. That is not an Eagle partnership. Book from 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport SK2 5DE, on 07517 806082 or icomplypropertyservices@gmail.com.

Cold mornings make an Eagle raise slower, and we write the weather next to the seconds so a summer visit is not compared with a January one unfairly. Three Eagle cycles are timed with the lane empty. If a van clips the Eagle arm and a car does not, the van is the vehicle we set to, and the quote says that. The Eagle safety edge or photocell that stops the boom is tested with an object the site can see, not with a hand waved at the last moment as we leave.

Eagle yards often have the photocell wrapped because a trailer parks in the beam. The trailer is the reason on the note, and the Eagle beam is re-aimed only if they can park the trailer somewhere else. We do not condemn an Eagle gearbox because the beam was blocked. The Eagle arm is returned to the position the yard uses, and the person who locks up signs nothing we have not shown them. If a second Eagle lane is on the same site, it is a second quote unless they have asked for both in the same instruction.
frontier-pitts: Frontier Pitts work may be a gate leaf, a rising arm or a vehicle blocker. Those are different foundations. The quote says which Frontier Pitts product is in the ground.
A Frontier Pitts leaf that drags is a hinge, a dropped pier or a closer, and we say which. We do not price a new Frontier Pitts leaf because the existing one scrapes.

Hostile-vehicle products from Frontier Pitts are not treated as a car-park arm. The survey includes the approach, the foundation and the duty the site thinks it has. We do not invent a rating the product does not have.
Keys and override handles for a Frontier Pitts gate are counted with the site manager. Missing Frontier Pitts keys are listed. We do not supply a lookalike padlock and call the leaf secure.

Frontier Pitts leaves are heavy. A dragging Frontier Pitts gate is a pier measurement with a tape, not a guess from the road. We record the gap under the Frontier Pitts leaf at the latch and at the hinge. Blockers in the Frontier Pitts range are quoted with the foundation that is visible, and we do not claim a security rating the casting does not show. If a Frontier Pitts closer is missing its cover, the quote includes the cover only when the manager wants it, not as a surprise extra.
heald: Heald HT1 and HT2 cabinets are easy to confuse from across the lane. We read the Heald plate at the hinge side of the door. The HT number decides the boom kit.
A Heald arm that chatters at the end of travel is adjusted on the limits, not by bending the Heald boom. The limit screws are marked before they are moved so they can be put back.
Heald loops set in block paving are tested for continuity before the paving is lifted. If the Heald loop is healthy, the fault is in the cabinet and the paving stays down.
The Heald note includes the direction of travel, in or out, because an exit Heald lane and an entry Heald lane do not share a loop setting.

Heald HT1 and Heald HT2 share a family look and not a parts list. The Heald plate is read with the door open and the characters are copied in full, including any suffix. Limits on a Heald cabinet are marked with a pencil before a screwdriver touches them, so a wrong adjustment can be undone. Block paving over a Heald loop stays put when the continuity reading is sound. Entry Heald lanes and exit Heald lanes are named on the note because their loop sensitivity is not the same setting.

A Heald boom that has been shortened on site is measured before a replacement is ordered. The Heald spring that suited the original length will not suit a cut-down arm, and we say so rather than forcing the old spring. The Heald cabinet door seal is checked because a wet Heald board is a different job from a noisy Heald gearbox. We write the Heald direction, the plate and the loop reading on one note so the next visit does not open the paving again. If the Heald arm clears cars but clips a high van, the van is the vehicle we set to, and the quote says that.

Heald parts are identified from the plate, not from a photograph taken across the car park. We do not claim a Heald partnership. CAME is the barrier partner we specify when a lane is being built new. A Heald barrier that is already in the ground is serviced or replaced on its own quote. The price is on application after the lane, the HT number and the safety devices are known. You get that quote before the Heald lane is taken out of use. The person who locks the yard is shown the Heald release, and they operate it once before we leave.
hysecurity: HySecurity equipment on these pages is the hydraulic barrier, not a sliding gate from a different range unless the plate says so. Hydraulic oil, hoses and the HySecurity motor temperature are the first checks.
A HySecurity arm that creeps down overnight is a hydraulic hold, and we measure how far it drops. That measurement is the reason a seal is quoted, not a guess from the phone call.
Cold mornings change a HySecurity raise time. We record the temperature and the seconds. A slow HySecurity raise in a frost is not automatically a failed pump.
The HySecurity manual release is a procedure, not a hidden valve for us to leave half open. The site contact operates it once while we watch.

HySecurity hydraulics are slow to forgive a low oil level. We check the HySecurity reservoir before running repeated tests, and we write the level rather than topping it up in silence. Creep is measured in millimetres over twenty minutes with the HySecurity arm at the parked angle the site uses by day. A frosty morning is noted beside the HySecurity raise time so a summer visit is not compared with a winter one unfairly. The person who will use the HySecurity manual release turns it themselves. We do not leave a valve cracked open.

Hose weep on a HySecurity cabinet is photographed against the serial plate before a seal kit is named. We do not wipe the HySecurity oil away and call the lane healthy. The HySecurity motor temperature after three raises is written next to the seconds, because a hot HySecurity motor with a normal raise is a different finding from a slow cold raise. Filters and breathers are on the quote only when they are dirty. A clean HySecurity reservoir is said to be clean.

HySecurity equipment already on a private lane is serviced or replaced. That is not a HySecurity partnership. CAME is the partner we specify when the lane is new. The HySecurity quote names the arm, the hydraulic hold and whether the safety devices still stop the boom. Price is on application after that survey. The lane is given back in the position the site uses, and the note of the oil level and the raise time stays with the building so the next HySecurity visit starts from a measurement rather than from a phone call.
life: Life SUPRA and Life GEAR operators are different machines. The Life badge and the operator cover decide which one is on the quote. A photograph of the Life cover from above is the useful one.

A Life operator that hums and does not drive the boom is isolated before the cover comes off. Capacitor and limit checks are written as readings, not as 'Life motor replaced' when the motor was not changed.
Life booms supplied with a skirt are weighed into the spring choice. Removing a Life skirt to make the arm faster is not a repair we do without saying so.
The Life handover is the cover refitted and the lane tested with a car the site provides. We do not test a Life lane by walking the loop.

Life SUPRA covers and Life GEAR covers do not interchange, so the photograph we want is square-on to the Life lid. A humming Life operator is isolated at the local switch before the lid comes off, and the readings that follow are numbers, not a story about a burnt Life motor unless the motor was actually changed. Skirts supplied with a Life boom stay on for the spring check. The test at the end is a car the site moves across the Life loop. Walking the loop is not the test we sign.

Life SUPRA and Life GEAR are different machines, and the cover decides which one is on the quote. A photograph of the Life lid from above is the one that helps, because the badges on the side are often faded and the two covers do not interchange. We do not order a Life SUPRA part for a Life GEAR operator because the boom looks similar from the road. The Life model is copied from the plate with the cover open, including any suffix.

A Life operator that hums and does not drive the boom is isolated at the local switch before the cover comes off. Capacitor and limit checks are written as readings. We do not write 'Life motor replaced' when the motor was not changed. A humming Life motor can be a capacitor, a limit that never makes, or a gearbox that has seized. Those are different quotes. The reading is what the next visit starts from, so the same Life cover is not taken off to discover the same number again.

Life booms supplied with a skirt are weighed into the spring choice. Removing a Life skirt to make the arm faster is not a repair we do without saying so. A site that wants the skirt off for clearance under a loading bay door is told the Life spring may then be too strong, and the quote includes the spring change if that is the case. The skirt stays on for the test unless they have agreed it comes off.

The Life handover is the cover refitted and the lane tested with a car the site provides. We do not test a Life lane by walking the loop and calling it proved. Walking the loop can satisfy a detector that a low car will miss, and it does not show whether the Life arm clears the roof of the vehicle they actually use. The car is moved by their driver. We time the raise and the drop and write both.

Life equipment already on a private lane is serviced or replaced. That is not a Life partnership. CAME is the barrier partner we specify when the lane is new. The Life quote names the operator, the spring and whether the safety devices still stop the boom. Price is on application after the cover, the skirt and the loop have been seen. You get that quote before the Life lane is taken out of use. The office is 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport SK2 5DE. Phone 07517 806082 or email icomplypropertyservices@gmail.com.

If the Life cover screws are rusted, we say so before they are drilled, because a lost Life cover is a separate line from the operator fault. The Life manual release is shown to the person who locks the lane, and they operate it once. We do not leave a Life release that needs a tool they do not have. Power to the Life operator is identified before any terminal is touched, and a dark Life display is not described as a dead gearbox until that supply has been checked.

A Life barrier that shares a post with a pedestrian gate is quoted with the gate named separately. We do not take the gate off to make the Life boom look straight. The Life loop tails are labelled before they are lifted, and a loop that has been paved over is a civils conversation rather than a promise made from the car park. If the Life arm clears cars but clips a high van, the van is the vehicle we set to. The Life cabinet key is returned to the person who met us. Three Life cycles are timed with the lane empty and the seconds are written next to the weather, so a cold morning is not later described as a failed Life pump.
newgate: Newgate barriers on private estates are often the only control the residents trust. The Newgate arm speed is agreed with the estate, because a fast Newgate drop frightens drivers who use that entrance every day.
A Newgate lock that will not throw is the lock, the keep or the alignment of the Newgate post. We say which. Packing a Newgate keep with washers is written on the note if that is what held.
Estate fobs that release a Newgate lane are tested with a resident's fob if they offer it. We do not clone a Newgate fob.
The Newgate quote states whether the LED strip on the arm is included. A dark Newgate boom at night is a lighting fault, separate from the gearbox.

Newgate arms on housing estates are seen by the same drivers every day, so the drop speed is a conversation, not a factory default we refuse to discuss. A Newgate keep that misses the lock is measured for alignment against the Newgate post before any washer is added, and if a washer is what holds, the note says washer. Resident fobs are borrowed and handed back. We do not copy a Newgate token. A dark Newgate boom is quoted as lighting only when they ask for light, and the gearbox price is not used to hide that.

Newgate arms on private estates are seen by the same drivers every day, so the drop speed is a conversation with the estate, not a factory default we refuse to discuss. A fast Newgate drop frightens people who use that entrance with children in the car. We time the drop with the lane empty and agree a speed they will live with. If the Newgate operator cannot slow to that speed without a different setting or a different arm, the quote says which.

A Newgate lock that will not throw is the lock, the keep or the alignment of the Newgate post. We say which. Packing a Newgate keep with washers is written on the note if that is what held, including how many washers, so the next visit does not treat a packed keep as a failed lock. A Newgate post that has moved is a ground problem. We do not keep adding washers until the Newgate lock just catches and then call the gate sound.

Estate fobs that release a Newgate lane are tested with a resident's fob if they offer it. The fob is handed back. We do not clone a Newgate fob, and we do not take a fob away to 'program it at the office'. If the Newgate reader accepts one fob and refuses another, both results are written with the time, and the reader is not condemned from a single refusal. The estate tells us which fob is supposed to work.

The Newgate quote states whether the LED strip on the arm is included. A dark Newgate boom at night is a lighting fault, separate from the gearbox. We do not fold a lighting request into a gearbox price. If they want light and the gearbox is healthy, the quote is the light. If the Newgate gearbox is the fault and they also want light, they are two lines. The estate can accept one and refuse the other.

Newgate equipment already on an estate is serviced or replaced. That is not a Newgate partnership. CAME is the partner we specify when a lane is being built new. Price is on application after the arm speed, the lock and the fob reader have been seen. You get the quote before the Newgate lane is taken out of use. The person who locks the estate is shown the Newgate release and operates it once. The office is 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport SK2 5DE. Paving against a Newgate post is photographed where it has lifted, because a lifted slab can push the post far enough to miss the keep. We do not quote a new Newgate leaf because a slab has risen. The gap under the Newgate arm at the closed position is measured, and a van that clips it is the vehicle named on the note. Residents who walk dogs through the Newgate line are asked which hour is quiet enough for a test, and we wait for that hour rather than running the arm through people.

Newgate loops set in block paving are tested for continuity before the paving is lifted. A healthy Newgate loop means the fault is in the cabinet and the paving stays down. The Newgate note includes the direction of travel, because an entry lane and an exit lane do not share a sensitivity. If the Newgate arm has been shortened on site, it is measured before a replacement is ordered, and the old spring is not forced onto the shorter arm. The Newgate door seal is checked, because a wet board is a different job from a noisy gearbox. Limits are marked before they are moved so a wrong adjustment can be undone.

SKIDATA staff talk in device names from their screen. We copy that SKIDATA name onto our note before the barrier housing is opened. SKIDATA power is identified before a cover comes off, because a dark screen and a still arm are different faults and the quote says which one we found. A SKIDATA lane closed with a cone is reopened only when the safety loop sees a vehicle again, and the operator watches one exit with us. We do not park a SKIDATA arm upright overnight unless the manager has asked for that. The free-exit loop, where the lane has one, is tested with a car at walking pace. Shift reports are compared with the time on the rejected ticket before any SKIDATA part is blamed. The housing is closed and the key is handed back.

fire-ready: Fire Ready is a life-safety pack for a commercial building that already has some of the systems fitted. It is not a catalogue of equipment and it is not the Compliance Bundle. The Compliance Bundle is the published residential pack at £561. Fire Ready is price on application after the scope is known. The written quote names which systems are in the building and which visits are included. Nothing is added on the day because a panel turned out to be a different brand.

A typical Fire Ready instruction covers a fire alarm service to BS 5839 where an alarm is fitted, an emergency lighting test to BS 5266 where fittings exist, and a check of automatic opening vents and smoke control where those are installed. Smoke and carbon monoxide devices are included where the building has them and the instruction asks for them. An optional fire risk assessment liaison is a separate line if the responsible person wants the papers read against the systems, not a silent extra.

AOV and smoke control inside Fire Ready are fire protection. Where the building is outside the North West, the smoke-vent visit can still be quoted, and the travel sits on that quote rather than being discovered after the engineer has arrived. The quote says which vents, which panel and which stair. A vent that has been screwed shut is reported to the responsible person before it is released. We do not open a vent that the building has deliberately fixed without telling them.

The certification pack is what the insurer or the auditor usually asks to see: what was tested, what passed, what failed and the date. Fire Ready does not promise a pass. A detector that fails, a luminaire that does not last the duration, or a vent that does not open is written as a fail, and the remedial is its own quote. We do not fold a replacement panel into the service price.

England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland do not share one building-regulations text. The Fire Ready note says which nation's building the visit was for, and it does not describe a Scottish block as if it were an English one. The responsible person tells us who the enforcing authority is if an audit is already open. We do not contact that authority unless they ask us to.

Booking Fire Ready starts with the address, the systems that are fitted, and whether the building will be occupied. Send that to icomplypropertyservices@gmail.com or call or WhatsApp 07517 806082. The confirmation itemises the systems and says the price is on application. VAT is shown on that confirmation.

That residential instruction is the Compliance Bundle or the Landlord pack, both published at £561 where the scope matches. A shop, an office or a block with an alarm and smoke vents is the Fire Ready conversation. The Fire Ready file comes back as one set for that address. Questions about a code are answered against that file. We do not rewrite a fail into a pass because the audit is next week. A follow-on repair is a new instruction with its own price. If a second building is mentioned in the same email, it is not silently added. Each address keeps its own Fire Ready quote.

Batteries on a fire alarm or a smoke-control panel are load-tested on a Fire Ready visit, not merely measured at rest. A panel that has run for months on mains with a tired battery can show only a small fault lamp, and the vents or the sounders will not run when the mains fails. The result for each battery is on the certificate. Cable that has been replaced with ordinary cable on a smoke-control circuit is listed so it can be put right. We do not describe that cable as acceptable because the vent opened on the day of the test.

Weekly user tests stay with the building. Fire Ready is the competent visit, not a replacement for the log the staff already keep. We ask to see that log so a fault that has been written there for months is not a surprise on the day. If there is no log, the certificate says so. The next Fire Ready date is proposed in the file, and it is a suggestion until the responsible person agrees it.
